title: Applications of derivatives in finding rate of change
competency: Solve problems where quantities change with time.

keywords.def: Rates of change with time of quantities linked by one formula.
The rate of change of displacement with time: v = dS/dt.

en.text: When two quantities are linked by a formula and both change with time, differentiate the formula with respect to t using the chain rule (A = πr² gives dA/dt = 2πr dr/dt). Put in the numbers for that instant only after differentiating. Velocity is dS/dt and acceleration is dv/dt.

am.text: ሁለት መጠኖች በቀመር ሲያያዙና ሁለቱም በጊዜ ሲለወጡ ቀመሩን በ t እንዋጽኦ (dA/dt = 2πr dr/dt)። ቁጥሮቹን ከዋጽኦ በኋላ እናስገባለን።

screens.title: A spreading circle
screens.ask: The radius of a circle grows 1.5 cm every second. Does the area grow by the same amount each second?
opts: No, it grows faster as the circle gets bigger
screens.after:
A = πr², so dA/dt = 2πr × dr/dt.
The area gained each second depends on r.
At r = 1: 2π(1)(1.5) = 3π cm²/s. At r = 10: 30π cm²/s.
A bigger circle has a longer edge, so it gains more area each second.
screens.best: No, it grows faster as the circle gets bigger

screens.title: Watch dA/dt grow with r
screens.ask: The radius grows at dr/dt = 1.5 cm/s. Move r and watch the rate of the area.
screens.note: The rate dr/dt stays 1.5, but dA/dt = 3πr grows with r. At r = 6, dA/dt = 18π ≈ 56.55 cm²/s.

screens.title: Related rates
paras: If two variables are related, their rates of change with time are related too.
Write the formula, differentiate both sides with respect to t, then substitute.
screens.note: Velocity v = dS/dt. Acceleration a = dv/dt.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Rates of change with time of quantities linked by one formula.
The rate of change of displacement with time: v = dS/dt.

screens.text: Related rates for a circle: dr/dt = 1.5 cm/s. When the diameter is 12 cm, find dA/dt.
screens.why:
Formula: A = πr².
Differentiate with respect to t: dA/dt = 2πr × dr/dt.
The diameter is 12, so r = 6 (not 12).
dA/dt = 2π(6)(1.5) = 18π cm²/s.
Trap: using r = 12 gives 36π, double the answer.
screens.clue: Use the radius, half the diameter.

screens.title: A balloon gets 4 cm³/min of air. Find dr/dt at r = 2 cm

screens.text: Put the steps for solving a related-rates problem in order.
items: Write the formula that links the quantities
Differentiate both sides with respect to t
Substitute the values at that instant
screens.why:
1. Write the formula first (A = πr², V = (4/3)πr³, Pythagoras …).
2. Differentiate with respect to t, using the chain rule.
3. Only now put in the numbers for that instant.
4. Solve for the rate you want.
Trap: substituting before differentiating makes the variable a constant, and its rate becomes 0.
screens.clue: Numbers go in only after you differentiate.

screens.ask: Velocity from displacement: S = t³ − 3t² + 5t + 7 (km, t in hours). Velocity at t = 2 is ___ km/h
screens.why:
Velocity is v = dS/dt.
v = 3t² − 6t + 5 (the constant 7 gives 0).
At t = 2: 3(4) − 6(2) + 5 = 12 − 12 + 5.
v = 5 km/h.

screens.ask: Acceleration from velocity: for the same S = t³ − 3t² + 5t + 7, acceleration at t = 2 is ___ km/h²
screens.why:
Acceleration is a = dv/dt.
v = 3t² − 6t + 5, so a = 6t − 6.
At t = 2: 6(2) − 6 = 6.
a = 6 km/h².
Trap: do not differentiate S only once; a needs the second derivative.

screens.ask: Related rates on a path: a point moves on 3y = x². dx/dt = 2 ft/min when x = 6. Find dy/dt = ___ ft/min
screens.why:
Differentiate both sides with respect to t.
3 dy/dt = 2x dx/dt (chain rule on x²).
Substitute x = 6, dx/dt = 2: 3 dy/dt = 2(6)(2) = 24.
dy/dt = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 ft/min.
screens.clue: Differentiate both sides with respect to t.

screens.ask: Related rates for a square plate: the side grows 0.2 cm/s. When the side is 20 cm, dA/dt = ___ cm²/s
screens.why:
Formula: A = s².
Differentiate: dA/dt = 2s × ds/dt.
Substitute s = 20, ds/dt = 0.2.
dA/dt = 2(20)(0.2) = 8 cm²/s.

screens.ask: Related rates for a sphere: the volume grows 0.2π cm³/s. When r = 10 cm, dr/dt = ___ cm/s
screens.why:
Formula: V = (4/3)πr³.
Differentiate: dV/dt = 4πr² × dr/dt.
Substitute: 0.2π = 4π(10)² dr/dt = 400π dr/dt.
dr/dt = 0.2π ÷ 400π = 0.0005 cm/s.
Check: π cancels, so the answer has no π.

screens.ask: Shadow problem: a man 2 m tall walks at 8 m/min away from a 6 m lamp post. His shadow grows at ___ m/min
screens.why:
Let x = his distance from the post, s = shadow length.
Similar triangles: 6/(x + s) = 2/s.
Cross-multiply: 6s = 2x + 2s, so 4s = 2x and s = x/2.
Differentiate: ds/dt = (1/2) dx/dt = (1/2)(8).
ds/dt = 4 m/min. It does not depend on where he is.
screens.clue: Set up similar triangles with base x + s.

items.text: Extreme values on a closed interval: f(x) = 3x + 2 on [3, 7]. Pick the smallest and the largest value.
items.why:
f(x) = 3x + 2 is increasing (slope 3 > 0).
So the smallest value is at the left end, the largest at the right end.
f(3) = 9 + 2 = 11. f(7) = 21 + 2 = 23.
Trap: 9 and 21 forget the + 2.

items.text: Extreme values on an open interval: f(x) = 3x + 2 on (3, 7). What is the smallest value?
items.why:
(3, 7) does not contain x = 3.
f gets close to 11 as x → 3, but never reaches it.
Any value you name, like 11.01, has a smaller one after it.
So there is no smallest value.
Trap: 11 is the answer only for the closed interval [3, 7].

items.text: Rate of change of a circle's area: dr/dt = 0.3 cm/s and r = 15 cm. Find dA/dt.
items.why:
A = πr², so dA/dt = 2πr × dr/dt.
dA/dt = 2π(15)(0.3).
2 × 15 = 30, and 30 × 0.3 = 9.
dA/dt = 9π cm²/s.
Trap: 4.5π forgets the 2 in 2πr.

items.ask: Rate of change of a sphere's radius: dV/dt = 0.2π cm³/s and r = 10 cm. dr/dt = ___ cm/s
items.why:
V = (4/3)πr³, so dV/dt = 4πr² × dr/dt.
0.2π = 4π(100) dr/dt = 400π dr/dt.
dr/dt = 0.2 ÷ 400 = 0.0005 cm/s.

items.ask: Rate of change of a square's area: ds/dt = 0.2 cm/s and s = 20 cm. dA/dt = ___ cm²/s
items.why:
A = s², so dA/dt = 2s × ds/dt.
dA/dt = 2(20)(0.2) = 8 cm²/s.

items.ask: Shadow rate: lamp post 6 m, man 2 m, walking speed 8 m/min. The shadow grows at ___ m/min
items.why:
Similar triangles: 6/(x + s) = 2/s.
6s = 2x + 2s, so s = x/2.
ds/dt = (1/2) dx/dt = (1/2)(8) = 4 m/min.

items.ask: Force and acceleration: a unit mass (m = 1 kg); the force grows 2 N/s. The acceleration grows ___ m/s² per second
items.why:
Newton's law: F = ma, so a = F/m = F (m = 1).
Differentiate with respect to t: da/dt = dF/dt.
da/dt = 2 m/s² per second.

test.ask: Rate of change of a square's area: A = s², ds/dt = 3 cm/s. At s = 5 cm, dA/dt = ___ cm²/s
test.why:
dA/dt = 2s × ds/dt.
Substitute s = 5, ds/dt = 3.
dA/dt = 2(5)(3) = 30 cm²/s.

test.ask: Velocity from displacement: S = 4t² + t (m). Velocity at t = 3 s is ___ m/s
test.why:
v = dS/dt = 8t + 1.
At t = 3: 8(3) + 1 = 25.
v = 25 m/s.
Trap: S(3) = 39 is the position, not the velocity.

test.ask: Acceleration from displacement: S = t³ (m). Acceleration at t = 2 s is ___ m/s²
test.why:
v = dS/dt = 3t².
a = dv/dt = 6t.
At t = 2: a = 12 m/s².
Trap: v(2) = 12 too here, but only by chance: always differentiate twice.

test.text: Rate of change of a circle's area: dr/dt = 2 cm/s. At r = 5 cm, find dA/dt.
test.why:
A = πr², so dA/dt = 2πr × dr/dt.
dA/dt = 2π(5)(2) = 20π cm²/s.
Trap: 10π forgets dr/dt = 2; 25π is the area itself.

test.ask: Related rates: y = x³ and dx/dt = 2 when x = 1. Find dy/dt = ___
test.why:
Differentiate with respect to t: dy/dt = 3x² × dx/dt.
Substitute x = 1, dx/dt = 2.
dy/dt = 3(1)²(2) = 6.

notes.text: Example 3 (p.114) prints "2 × √3/4 = 4√3": the substitution s = 4, ds/dt = 2 is missing. Correct: 2(4)(√3/4)(2) = 4√3 cm²/s.

screens.title: d/dt (r²) when r changes with t

screens.why:
Outside: s³ → 3s².
Inside: s depends on t, so multiply by ds/dt.
d/dt (s³) = 3s² ds/dt.
Trap: 3s² alone forgets the inner rate.
screens.clue: Do not forget the inner rate.
